chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Abu Jameela, who said:

I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so he said to me: 'O youth, what is your profession?' I said, 'The slaves (or servants).' He said: 'I advise you with an advice, so memorize it: Do not buy anything with a defect, nor a defect, and ensure the contract.'
ai.seo_question: What are the key conditions for buying slaves or servants according to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) provides specific commercial jurisprudence to a young man in the slave trade, emphasizing the prevention of disputes by avoiding hidden defects ('ayb) and ensuring the robustness of contractual obligations ('ahd). This advice reflects the broader Shia emphasis on transparency and fairness in market transactions, ensuring that the buyer is fully protected against future claims of defect or breach of contract.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Hameed, from Abu Jameela who said,

‘I went over to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘O youth! Which thing is your profession?’ So I said, ‘The slaves’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> advise you with an adive, so memorise it. Neither buy anything with a deformity, nor a defact, and affirm the contracts’.
en.sarwar: 18. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Hamid from abu Jamilah who has said the following:

“Once I visited abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and he asked, ‘Young man, what you do for a living?’ I replied, ‘It is slaves.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘I recommend you so keep my recommendations safe. You must not buy physically or morally defective ones. You must make the guarantees strong and firm.’”
